the-merge.lead: On 15 September 2022, Ethereum completed The Merge, joining its existing Mainnet execution layer to the Beacon Chain's proof-of-stake consensus system. The work had been years in preparation. Launched on 1 December 2020, the Beacon Chain had operated alongside Mainnet, establishing its validator network while the original chain continued handling transactions under proof-of-work. Two systems were ready to become one.

ftx-falls.lead: On 11 November 2022, FTX Trading Ltd. and numerous affiliated companies entered voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in Delaware. The filings covered a network of businesses, including entities behind FTX's international and US exchanges and Alameda Research, rather than one company alone. John J. Ray III took over as chief executive following Sam Bankman-Fried's departure, with the task of preserving assets and maximising recoveries for customers and creditors.

ordinals-master-085.lead: On 20 January 2023, Casey Rodarmor announced that inscriptions were ready for Bitcoin mainnet with the release of ord 0.4.0. This card marks that public announcement, not the first experiment.

usdc-loses-its-peg.lead: During 10–13 March 2023, USDC's promise of dollar stability faced a banking-system shock. Circle had $3.3 billion of its reserves at Silicon Valley Bank, about 8% of the total. Uncertainty about access to those funds helped push USDC below its dollar peg. Reserves caught in a failed bank were not the same as reserves proven permanently lost.

the-arbitrum-airdrop.lead: On 23 March 2023, eligible users could begin claiming ARB, the governance token associated with the Arbitrum DAO. Eligibility reflected activity recorded before a 6 February snapshot. This was a token-distribution and governance milestone, not the launch of the network: Arbitrum had already been operating on mainnet for nearly eighteen months.

pepe-returns.lead: In April and May 2023, PEPE brought a familiar internet frog into a new meme-token cycle. This was a fungible token on Ethereum, not a revival of the earlier Rare Pepe collectible series. Its enormous stated supply, 420,690,000,000,000 tokens, became part of the project's deliberately meme-heavy identity.

the-xrp-ruling.lead: On 13 July 2023, Judge Analisa Torres issued a mixed summary-judgment ruling in SEC v. Ripple Labs in the Southern District of New York. Ripple's institutional sales of XRP under written contracts constituted unregistered offers and sales of investment contracts. The result depended on the circumstances of those transactions.

binance-settles.lead: On 21 November 2023, Binance pleaded guilty in the United States to federal charges involving anti-money-laundering requirements, unlicensed money transmission and sanctions violations. The company agreed to a Justice Department resolution totaling $4,316,126,163: $2,510,650,588 in forfeiture and a $1,805,475,575 criminal fine. The total belonged to Binance, rather than its founder personally, and combined different forms of financial penalty.

spot-bitcoin-etfs-approved.lead: On 10 January 2024, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved exchange rule changes for eleven spot Bitcoin exchange-traded product proposals in one order, Release 34-99306. The decision opened a route to listing and trading shares on regulated U.S. exchanges. It did not approve Bitcoin itself or endorse it as an investment. The first wave began trading the following day, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust on Nasdaq.

dencun.lead: On 13 March 2024, Ethereum activated Dencun at epoch 269568. Its best-known change was EIP-4844, or proto-danksharding, which introduced temporary data blobs for rollups. These layer-2 networks process transactions away from Ethereum mainnet and publish data back to it. Blobs gave them a dedicated way to make that data available, designed to reduce a major operating cost and help lower fees for their users.

the-fourth-halving.lead: On 20 April 2024, Bitcoin reached block 840,000 and its fourth halving. The new-coin subsidy fell from 6.25 to 3.125 BTC per block. Between the first and fourth milestones, the 2016 halving had reduced it from 25 to 12.5 BTC, and the 2020 halving from 12.5 to 6.25 BTC. Each step followed another 210,000 blocks.

This was a partial distribution process, not an announcement that every creditor had received funds or been made whole.
